tasks.title: FR-006 Deep loop orchestration contract
tasks.description: Beacon must support `deep` as a loop-capable human support skill/toolkit surface that can iterate across PRD, user-story, test-case, implement evidence, QA evidence, and release evidence without becoming a new main lifecycle stage. Each `deep run` should execute the smallest complete loop required for the current user intent: ```text scan_truth -> model_business -> challenge_gaps -> derive_delta -> classify_findings -> route_repairs -> verify_closure ``` The default target is one-pass closure. A `deep run` should continue internally until it either closes all findings for the current intent or routes accepted deltas into the correct Beacon surface.

tasks.title: FR-010 Deep QA-preflight contract
tasks.description: Deep test deltas should be usable as a pre-QA iterative evolution surface. Before QA, deep may derive missing cases from PRD, user stories, state machines, fact-source maps, and existing test cases. After QA, deep may consume defects and evidence to decide whether the issue is a normal bug, a requirement gap, a state-machine gap, a test gap, or a release risk. ## 5A. Artifact Contract ### 5.1 Deep Analysis Report Path: ```text docs/beacon/<version>/deep/<feature>-deep-analysis.md ``` Required content: feature summary role model entity model main business closure cross-story invariant candidates fact-source and derived-field map deep findings proposed next actions ### 5.2 State Machine Report Path: ```text docs/beacon/<version>/deep/<feature>-state-machine.md ``` Required content: state list allowed transition matrix forbidden transition matrix actor/action/API trigger map transition invariants idempotency expectations ### 5.3 Deep Test Delta Path: ```text docs/beacon/<version>/qa/test-cases/<feature>-deep-delta.md ``` Required content per case: delta id linked user story or requirement area linked deep finding scenario expected result automation candidate gate classification: `MVP | Deep | Release | Backlog` severity: `P0 | P1 | P2 | P3` release blocking: `true | false` ### 5.4 Risk Register Path: ```text docs/beacon/<version>/deep/<feature>-risk-register.md ``` Required content: risk id description affected surfaces severity release blocking status owner or stage handling: `fix | test-delta | waiver | backlog | reject` ### 5.5 Deep Closure Brief Path: ```text docs/beacon/<version>/execution/deep-closure-brief-<feature>.md ``` Required content: deep requirement state deep verdict executed delta cases open findings waived findings accepted backlog risks release recommendation ### 5.6 Deep Loop Trace Path: ```text docs/beacon/<version>/deep/<feature>-deep-loop-trace.md ``` Required content: user intent snapshot loop iteration list discovered role/entity/state/process changes finding classification route decision for each finding closure decision stop reason next allowed route The trace is the audit bridge proving that deep loop converged or intentionally routed work back into Beacon's existing surfaces. ## 6. Command Surface The first implementation should expose one support entry, a human skill, and optional subcommands. Human skill: ```text beacon-deep ``` Minimum: ```bash beacon deep run "<feature>" --project-root . --version <version> ``` Recommended subcommands: ```bash beacon deep analyze "<feature>" --project-root . --version <version> beacon deep state-machine "<feature>" --project-root . --version <version> beacon deep derive-tests "<feature>" --project-root . --version <version> beacon deep close-loop "<feature>" --project-root . --version <version> ``` `deep` is a support command family. It must not be presented as a new required lifecycle stage. `beacon deep run` is the preferred public entry because it can perform scan, model, challenge, derive, route, and closure verification in one guided loop. ## 6A. Deep Loop State Machine ```text not_started -> scanning -> modeling -> challenging -> deriving_delta -> routing -> verifying -> closed ``` Allowed reopening conditions: user introduces a new feature, role, business process, or state machine QA evidence exposes a structural requirement or state gap implementation evidence contradicts the deep model release evidence exposes an unclosed high-risk finding accepted test deltas reveal a new state or invariant Default stop conditions: no unclassified finding remains no open release-blocking finding remains all accepted deltas are routed all waivers and backlog decisions are explicit no new state machine or feature was introduced by the current prompt ## 6B. State Axes The first implementation must keep these state axes explicit through freeze readiness, implementation planning, QA coverage, and release evidence: `deep_loop_state`: `not_started | scanning | modeling | challenging | deriving_delta | routing | verifying | closed` `finding_state`: `candidate | classified | routed | closed | waived | backlog | rejected` `delta_state`: `proposed | accepted | attached_to_test_case | executed_by_qa | closed` `risk_state`: `open | release_blocking | waived | accepted_backlog | closed` `requirement_package_state`: `prd_only | three_piece_complete | frozen | implement_pending` These axes must not be compressed into one generic status field. ## 7. Gate Semantics Deep gate semantics should be additive: release may check deep closure for high-risk features release may accept explicit skip reason for low-risk features P0/P1/P2 release-blocking deep findings must be closed or waived backlog findings must not block release unless explicitly promoted Candidate reason codes: `deep_analysis_required` `deep_closure_missing` `deep_release_blocking_findings_open` `deep_skip_reason_missing` `deep_test_delta_unexecuted` `deep_loop_unclosed` `deep_delta_route_missing` `deep_new_state_machine_unclassified` ## 7A. 风险与缓解 | 风险 | 影响 | 缓解 | |---|---|---| | deep 变成新的主阶段 | 破坏 Beacon 极简主流程 | 明确 deep 是 support surface，并要求 skip reason / trigger rule | | deep 直接改写 frozen truth | 破坏 canonical truth discipline | 所有 accepted finding 必须走 change/refreeze | | deep 与 QA 重复 | 扩大流程负担 | deep 只生成结构分析和 test delta，qa 负责执行 | | low-risk feature 被过度建模 | 降低交付效率 | 允许显式 skip reason，不默认阻塞 release | | backlog 风险误阻塞 release | release 判断噪音变高 | 风险分类必须区分 `Release` 与 `Backlog` | | deep loop 无限迭代 | 阻塞交付且削弱主流程心智 | 定义 one-pass closure、stop reason 和 allowed reopening conditions | | deep 发现无法路由 | finding 留在分析文档中失去执行价值 | 每个 finding 必须有 route decision 和 closure decision | ## 8A. Truth Governance Deep findings are not truth by themselves. The allowed path is: ```text deep finding -> supplement proposal -> human acceptance -> beacon change/refreeze -> updated PRD/user-story/test-case -> implementation/QA/release recheck ``` Deep may write supporting artifacts, but it may not directly mutate frozen PRD, user story, or test-case truth. ## 8. 验收标准 [ ] `v1.4.1` documents `deep` as support surface rather than a new lifecycle stage. [ ] High-risk trigger rules are documented. [ ] Skip reason semantics are documented. [ ] Deep artifact family is documented. [ ] Deep test delta format is documented. [ ] Release-facing deep closure semantics are documented. [ ] Deep findings are routed through change/refreeze before altering frozen truth. [ ] MVP / Deep / Release / Backlog classification is documented. [ ] First implementation can read PRD, user-story, test-case, QA progress, acceptance brief, and architecture blueprint when present. [ ] First implementation can produce at least deep analysis, state-machine report, test delta, and risk register. [ ] First implementation can produce a deep loop trace with iteration, route, closure, and stop reason. [ ] `beacon-deep` is described as a support skill/toolkit surface rather than a lifecycle stage. [ ] `beacon deep run` can converge scan/model/challenge/delta/route/verify in one run for the same user intent. [ ] Deep findings can route to PRD, user-story, test-case, implement repair, supplemental QA, release waiver, or backlog. [ ] Deep loop reopening requires a new user intent, feature, role, state machine, business process, or release-blocking evidence. [ ] Low-risk features can explicitly skip deep without release blockage. [ ] High-risk features without deep closure or skip decision can be surfaced as release risk. ## 10. Rollout Plan ### Phase 1: Documentation and manual sample Freeze this PRD. Produce one manual deep sample from `friend-match`. Validate artifact structure with human review. ### Phase 2: CLI generation Implement `beacon deep analyze`. Implement `beacon deep derive-tests`. Implement `beacon deep run` as the preferred one-pass loop orchestrator. Materialize `beacon-deep` as a host-visible support skill. Keep outputs as draft support artifacts. ### Phase 3: QA and release integration Let QA consume adopted deep deltas. Let QA defects re-enter deep only when they imply a structural state, fact-source, or requirement gap. Add deep closure brief generation. Add deep loop trace generation. Add release supplement checks for high-risk features. ### Phase 4: Governance hardening Add strict reason codes. Add skip reason verification. Add waiver handling for release-blocking deep findings. ## 11. Implementation Decisions `deep` will use its own support command family and human-facing support skill surface: `beacon-deep`. The first runtime implementation will treat the documented high-risk trigger categories as advisory diagnostics, then promote strict enforcement after implementation evidence proves stability. Human deep artifacts are required first; machine mirrors are allowed as compiled projections and audit evidence, not as a second truth root. Deep delta adoption routes through `test-case` for acceptance coverage gaps and through `change/refreeze` for requirement truth gaps. Release scorecards should reflect deep closure through closure brief presence, release-blocking finding status, waiver status, and backlog decision status. Internal toolkit modules stay hidden behind `beacon-deep` unless a later version proves that separate human surfaces reduce rather than increase operator friction. `deep_loop_unclosed`, `deep_delta_route_missing`, and `deep_new_state_machine_unclassified` start as explicit reason codes; strict gate promotion is deferred until implementation and QA evidence converge. ## 12. Final Requirement Statement Beacon `v1.4.1` must add a loop-capable deep analysis support capability that helps complex business features expose hidden state, transition, invariant, fact-source, and cross-module consistency risks. It must converge those risks into test deltas, route accepted gaps back into the existing Beacon lifecycle, and produce release evidence while preserving Beacon's small human lifecycle, canonical truth discipline, and support-surface boundaries.
